claims.text: Equiatomic NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC alloy.
Equiatomic NbMoTaW has limited room-temperature ductility.
Cold working by approximately 30–50% followed by annealing at 1000–1200 °C for 1–2 hours will form a fine, submicron, partially recrystallized microstructure in NbMoTaW.
A subsequent anneal at approximately 1400 °C for about one hour will stabilize dislocation networks.
The treatment will retain moderate dislocation density in a partially recrystallized BCC matrix containing subgrains.
Smaller grains and subgrain boundaries lower the activation barrier for low-temperature dislocation motion.
Easier initiation of dislocation slip will improve room-temperature ductility.
Subgrain boundaries and retained dislocation networks will act as sinks for irradiation-induced defects.
The retained subgrain and dislocation structure will preserve high-temperature strength.
The two-step thermomechanical treatment will increase room-temperature tensile elongation relative to untreated NbMoTaW.
The treated alloy will have comparable or moderately reduced room-temperature flow stress relative to untreated NbMoTaW.
The treatment will cause minimal change in yield strength at 1600 °C.
The treatment will sustain or enhance resistance to irradiation-induced damage.
NbMoTaW has yield strength above 400 MPa at 1600 °C.
NbMoTaW exhibits weak temperature dependence of yield strength from 600 °C to 1600 °C.
As-cast NbMoTaW has strong irradiation resistance predicted by first-principles calculations.
Excessive cold work or improperly timed annealing can produce grain structures that degrade room-temperature ductility or high-temperature performance.
Partial rather than complete recrystallization is required to obtain the proposed combination of properties.
